77970-how-to-save-money.title: How To Save Money
77970-how-to-save-money.creator: Unknown
77970-how-to-save-money.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Anyone in the income level above bare necessity who is not sufficiently interested in his or her own welfare to lay by a certain portion of earnings for the future either is irresponsible mentally or does not care what bitterness the future may bring. The creation of habit is a mechanical process. There is no mystery about it.

arxiv-2006-01579.title: Gauss Coordinates vs Currents for the Yangian Doubles of the Classical Types
arxiv-2006-01579.creator: Andrii LIASHYK † and Stanislav Z. PAKULIAK ‡
arxiv-2006-01579.description: Abstract We consider relations between Gauss coordinates of T T -operators for the Yangian doubles of the classical types corresponding to the algebras 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} of A A , B B , C C and D D series and the current generators of these algebras.

arxiv-2204-09373.title: On Lipschitz functions on groups equipped with conjugation-invariant norms
arxiv-2204-09373.creator: Jarek Kędra
arxiv-2204-09373.description: Abstract We observe that a function on a group equipped with a bi-invariant word metric is Lipschitz if and only if it is a partial quasimorphism bounded on the generating set. We also show that an undistorted element is always detected by an antisymmetric homogeneous partial quasimorphism.

arxiv-2206-01560.title: Magnetar Hard X-Ray Emission from Axion-like Particle Conversion
arxiv-2206-01560.creator: Jean-François Fortini i jean-francois.fortin@phy.ulaval.ca, Marianne Grattonii ii marianne.gratton.1@ulaval.ca
arxiv-2206-01560.description: Abstract We explore the possibility that axion-like-particles (ALPs), which would be produced in the core of magnetars and would then convert in the magnetosphere into photons, can explain magnetar hard X-ray spectra. We remark that this scenario would also provide answers to some questions related to magnetar heating.

arxiv-2408-10492.title: Is the Lecture Engaging? Lecture Sentiment Analysis for Knowledge Graph-Supported Intelligent Lecturing Assistant (ILA) System
arxiv-2408-10492.creator: Yuan An, Samarth Kolanupaka § , Jacob An § , Matthew Ma § , Unnat Chhatwal § , Alex Kalinowski, Michelle Rogers, Brian Smith
arxiv-2408-10492.description: Abstract This paper introduces an intelligent lecturing assistant (ILA) system that utilizes a knowledge graph to represent course content and optimal pedagogical strategies. The system is designed to support instructors in enhancing student learning through real-time analysis of voice, content, and teaching methods.

arxiv-2409-18462.title: Latent Representation Learning for Multimodal Brain Activity Translation
arxiv-2409-18462.creator: Arman Afrasiyabi 1,4,9 , Dhananjay Bhaskar 1,4,9 , Erica L. Busch 3,8,9 , Laurent Caplette 3,8,9 , Rahul Singh 1,8,9, Guillaume Lajoie 5,6,7 , Nicholas B. Turk-Browne 3,8,9,∗ , Smita Krishnaswamy 1,4,2,8,9,∗, Department of { 1 Computer Science, 2 Applied Mathematics, 3 Psychology, 4 Genetics, 5 Math
arxiv-2409-18462.description: Abstract Neuroscience employs diverse neuroimaging techniques, each offering distinct insights into brain activity, from electrophysiological recordings such as EEG, which have high temporal resolution, to hemodynamic modalities such as fMRI, which have increased spatial precision. However, integrating these heterogeneous data sources remains a challenge, which limits a comprehensive understanding of brain function.

arxiv-2504-13597.title: FocusNet: Transformer-enhanced Polyp Segmentation with Local and Pooling Attention
arxiv-2504-13597.creator: Jun Zeng 1 , KC Santosh 2 , Deepak Rajan Nayak 3 , Thomas de Lange 4 , Jonas Varkey 4 , Tyler Berzin 4 , Debesh Jha 2
arxiv-2504-13597.description: Abstract Colonoscopy is vital in the early diagnosis of colorectal polyps. Regular screenings can effectively prevent benign polyps from progressing to CRC. While deep learning has made impressive strides in polyp segmentation, most existing models are trained on single-modality and single-center data, making them less effective in real-world clinical environments.

arxiv-2509-24873.title: Uncertainty-Guided Expert-AI Collaboration for Efficient Soil Horizon Annotation DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: European Conference on Artificial Intelligence, CLEAR-AI Workshop: Collaborative Methods and Tools for Engineering and Evaluating Transparency in AI; October 25–30, 2025; Bologna, Italy
arxiv-2509-24873.creator: Teodor Chiaburu, Vipin Singh, Frank Haußer, Felix Bießmann
arxiv-2509-24873.description: Abstract . Uncertainty quantification is essential in human-machine collaboration, as human agents tend to adjust their decisions based on the confidence of the machine counterpart. Reliably calibrated model uncertainties, hence, enable more effective collaboration, targeted expert intervention and more responsible usage of Machine Learning (ML) systems.

arxiv-2510-13550.title: Exact dynamics and qubit inversion of non-Hermitian driven two-level systems
arxiv-2510-13550.creator: Ivan A. Bocanegra-Garay, Luis M. Nieto
arxiv-2510-13550.description: Abstract The supersymmetric structure of a generalized non-Hermitian driven two-level system is demonstrated. A unitary rotation turns the Hamiltonian into a more convenient form. After decoupling a set of differential equations, the supersymmetric structure of the problem can be unequivocally appreciated.

arxiv-2511-18370.title: MimiCAT: Mimic with Correspondence-Aware Cascade-Transformer for Category-Free 3D Pose Transfer
arxiv-2511-18370.creator: Zenghao Chai Chen Tang Yongkang Wong Xulei Yang Mohan Kankanhalli
arxiv-2511-18370.description: Abstract 3D pose transfer aims to transfer the pose-style of a source mesh to a target character while preserving both the target’s geometry and the source’s pose characteristic. Existing methods are largely restricted to characters with similar structures and fail to generalize to category-free settings ( e.g . , transferring a humanoid’s pose to a quadruped).

arxiv-2512-07795.title: ReasonBENCH: Benchmarking the (In)Stability of LLM Reasoning
arxiv-2512-07795.creator: Nearchos Potamitis, Lars Klein, Akhil Arora
arxiv-2512-07795.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in settings where reasoning, such as multi-step problem solving and chain-of-thought, is essential. Yet, current evaluation practices overwhelmingly report single-run accuracy while ignoring the intrinsic uncertainty that naturally arises from stochastic decoding.

pmc-11550753.title: “Investigating impact of Ni-Cd substitution on structural magnetic and optical properties of nanosize Al ferrites”
pmc-11550753.creator: Shikhil S. Wanjari, Deoram V. Nandanwar, K.G. Rewatkar, Amit V. Gongal
pmc-11550753.description: Ferrites are among the most extensively studied materials, specifically due to their amazing and diverse characteristics. Therefore, we synthesized NixCd1-xAlyFe2-yO4 (NCAF) ferrites using a microwave auto-combustion process, with x varying from 0.0 to 1.0 and y set at 0.1. We conducted a meticulous characterization of their structural, surface morphological, magnetic, molecular vibrational and optical properties.

pmc-11573365.title: Perceptions and practices of healthcare providers in providing HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis to trans adolescents and young adults and men who have sex with men
pmc-11573365.creator: Ayra Zaine Rodrigues Urbano, Dulce Ferraz, Yzabelle de Lima Raymundo, Eliana Miura Zucchi, Ayra Zaine Rodrigues Urbano, Dulce Ferraz, Yzabelle de Lima Raymundo, Eliana Miura Zucchi
pmc-11573365.description: OBJECTIVE:This study aims to understand the perceptions and practices of healthcare providers regarding the offer of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to gay and trans adolescents and young adults.METHODS:This qualitative research was developed as part of the PrEP1519 study, which was conducted from 2018 to 2021 to analyze the effectiveness of PrEP in adolescents and young adults.

pmc-11716762.title: Identification of stage‐specific blood biomarkers for early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease through RNA sequencing analysis
pmc-11716762.creator: Akiko Yamakawa, Mutsumi Suganuma, Risa Mitsumori, Shumpei Niida, Kouichi Ozaki, Daichi Shigemizu
pmc-11716762.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe detailed mechanism of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) has not been fully elucidated, and a comprehensive gene expression analysis of the entire process leading up to the onset of AD has never been conducted on a large scale.MethodWe performed RNA‐seq analysis of 1227 blood samples consisting of 424 AD, 543 mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 260 cognitive normal (CN) subjects, and examined differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between CN and MCI (CN‐MCI), and between MCI and AD (MCI‐AD).

pmc-13077672.title: Neurodivergent influenceability in agentic AI as a contingent solution to the AI alignment problem
pmc-13077672.creator: Alberto Hernández-Espinosa, Felipe S Abrahão, Olaf Witkowski, Hector Zenil, Derek Abbott
pmc-13077672.description: Ensuring that AI systems, including artificial general intelligence and artificial superintelligence, behave in alignment with human values and interests presents significant challenges and is known as the AI alignment problem. As AI advances, concerns about control and existential risks become increasingly relevant.

pmc-13081075.title: In Silico Destructive Activity of Phytochemicals From Ocimum sanctum Against the T9SS Proteins of Porphyromonas gingivalis
pmc-13081075.creator: Vishnudas H, Anjali Chaudhary, Kennedy Babu, Manoj Margabandhu, Lakshminarayanan S, Jawahar Raman L
pmc-13081075.description: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory condition closely associated with the pathogenic activity of Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis). Among its virulence components, the PorA and PorE proteins play essential roles in the type IX secretion system (T9SS), facilitating the release of gingipain-related factors that contribute to tissue destruction. Targeting these proteins may offer a promising therapeutic strategy.

uslaw-usc-t15-s2227.title: 15 U.S.C. § 2227 — Fire safety systems in federally assisted buildings
uslaw-usc-t15-s2227.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s2227.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 49 (Fire Prevention And Control). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Definitions For purposes of this section, the following definitions apply: (1) The term “affordable cost” means the cost to a Federal agency of leasing office space in a building that is protected by an automatic sprinkler system or equivalent level of safety.
